items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Gladys; the interviewer asks about her role in Lionel Hampton's finances, and the interviewee responds generally about 'your wife' without confirming Gladys is his wife or providing personal details about her.

ctx.x: Then Lawrence played -- Lionel Hampton was the drummer in the band and he worked there for many years with us. That's where I first got to be very good friends with Lionel Hampton. That's when he was deriving his style of playing two-finger piano and xylophones, vibraphones, actually, and then when Lionel formed his band in 1941, I formed his band, worked as his music director with him. I rehearsed his band, put it together for him, picked most of its men from this area out here. My brother, (ERNIE) was the lead…
Was he running the finances or was Gladys running the finances? (inaudible)?

Oh, yes. After all, it was his band. When your wife is running the finances, you got to say something about it. You know, you can't duck under too many skirts always, you know. People always try to find out different reasons why certain things don't happen. They can find excuses. But I formed his big band, put it together. He became a millionaire. Then, when I was in the service, after I left his band, he never even came by to take me out to dinner and I put his band together for him.
